title: Intelligence report from Port Sainte-Marie in numerical code, enclosed to the Duke of Newcastle, 1729 (Huntington Library mssBLA 191, p. 5)

documents.shelfmark: Huntington Library, Blathwayt papers addenda, mssBLA 191, p. 5 (HDL p15150coll7 61005)
documents.route: El Puerto de Santa María -> 'Cesnok' -> Duke of Newcastle

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaf; deciphered sibling enclosures in the same code are in mssBLA 187, 188 and the letters of 14 July and 4 Aug 1729.

transcription.source: HDL image 61005, IIIF region crops at full resolution
transcription.notes: Doubtful digits: L01 386, L02 1201, L03 163, L10 473 (the last settled by 14 July p. 3: 473 = faire).

system.summary: Numerical syllable-and-word nomenclator of about 1,300 groups, roughly alphabetical (syllables then words per letter), with homophones for a few words and unglossed stop groups.

prior_solution.where: Catalogue #826 (28 Oct 2026): no decipherment of p. 5 known; the sibling letters in the same code carry contemporary interlinear decipherments, which supplied the key.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution: johonn chose the target, set the rules and the plan (rebuild the code from the deciphered sibling letters, apply it to p. 5) and approved it. The transcription, table, decode and reading were done by Claude Code under their direction; no target-specific intervention.

solution.what: HDL CONTENTdm API listed the pages of mssBLA 191, 187, 188 and the letters of 14 July and 4 Aug 1729; all 39 page images fetched by IIIF.

Contact sheets of the 39 pages: code pages with a contemporary interlinear decipherment found on 60963, 60916-60920, 60886-60887 and 60907-60909; the interlinear values are syllables and short words, so the system is a syllable-and-word code.
Report (HDL 61005) transcribed from region crops: 13 lines, 141 groups, 101 distinct; four doubtful digits.
mssBLA 188 enclosure (HDL 60917-60920) transcribed: 56 code lines with the interlinear gloss under each group.
First code table from the 188 glosses applied to the report: 105 of 141 groups valued.
Letter of 14 July (60887, 19 passages) and letter of 4 Aug (60907-60909, 40 passages) transcribed; clear, dotted copies.
mssBLA 187 p. 3 (60963) transcribed; glosses not set under their groups, so alignment by position was unreliable and every pairing is marked doubtful.
Table read in group order: a roughly alphabetical syllable-and-word nomenclator (208 comme, 217 concert, 224 confidence ... 256 correspondance; numerals 1206-1213; T block not strictly ordered).
Table rebuilt (383 groups, 1,078 glossed groups); report decoded: 116 firm, 2 doubtful, 22 tokens open; French reading with holes checked against the table by reading.py.

Alphabetical bracketing of the open groups (slots.py): candidates 285 do, 1152 vos, 1210 six, 222 conduite, 805 obligation, 816 ordre, 585 ig, kept as [?word]; the weak guess 1152 = traite was dropped because its slot contradicts it.
Clear pages: the 21 July letter (61003-61004) and the 14 July clear text (60886) do not contain the report; 60886 repeats the 14 July extracts only.
docs/_validate.py could not run: the lang corpora (Gutenberg) were unreachable. validation.tsv is ready.

Issue #189 (Michael Brackx) taken in: glossed groups of mssBLA 185, 194, 179 added (transcription/sibbrackx189.txt); 188 gloss digits 737->937, 383->387, 1017->1019 corrected. Table rebuilt (420 groups); report decode 121 firm, 3 doubtful, 16 tokens open; reading.py consistent; _check_reading 2/9 clean sentences, hole rate 0.22.

The sibling pages not yet read (60915-60916, 60921-60922, 60903-60906, 60910-60912, 60961-60962, 60964) surveyed: no new glossed code; 60903-60904 is the clear copy of the coded 4 Aug letter, its bracketed passages transcribed and paired with the code lines of 60907-60908 (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Pre-registered held-out check (beling/PREREG.md): the code table rebuilt without the 4 Aug glosses, aligned to the 4 Aug clear copy, matches 158 of 170 tokens (0.929); 200 shuffled tables best 0.171, margin 0.759; pass. Eight table values confirmed or corrected from the clear copy (701 mo, 791 ois, 869 perdu, 880 plustot, 829 pl, 169 com, 900 pris, 191 c'est); none is in the report (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Value-finding for the 15 open groups from table order, homophone patterns and context (no held-out material): proposals 585 ig, 1152 vos, 285 do, 1210 six, 222 conduite, 805 obligation, 689 m, 1052 servi, 836 pr, 214 comte; 726, 460, 1118 weak; 711 and 6 open. Kept as [?word], not promoted (beling/results/open_group_values.md) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

mssBLA 194 (HDL 60893-60894), a letter wholly in the same code with interlinear decipherment, transcribed in full (beling/transcription/sib194_*.txt); pre-registered (beling/PREREG_round2.md): the table rebuilt without any 194 gloss matches 89 of 93 firm glosses (0.957; 200 shuffled tables best 0.065; pass). 1118, one of the report's open groups, is glossed 'tain' there (retouched); it does not yet give sense in the report (Andrew Beling, beling/).

60917 L02 and L17 re-read at full resolution: 369 (e), not 869; L16 830 (plus), not 880. 60909 placed as the code part of a later letter of 3 Nov 1729. Full construction: beling/results/full_table.tsv, one row per group (439) with every gloss and clear-copy attestation, 20 conflict rows; codetable.tsv not changed (Andrew Beling, beling/).

Print search for a clear text of the report: HMC Polwarth I-V (vol. V searched inside on HathiTrust: no 'Port St. Mary', 'cipher' or 'Cadiz'; 3 hits for 'Pareti'), Coxe's Kings of Spain and Walpole, TNA and BL catalogues: nothing. Marchmont's note of 8 Aug 1729 (61001) says the two letters he forwarded were of 14 and 21 July; the report is probably the coded part of the 21 July letter (inference) (Andrew Beling, beling/).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from the interlinear decipherments of the sibling letters in the same file (mssBLA 187, 188, 14 July, 4 Aug 1729) and applied to the report.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decryption/report_61005_decode.txt: 121 of 141 cipher tokens with a firm value; doubtful values, open groups and the stop group counted unread.

Issue #189: glossed groups from mssBLA 185, 194 and 179 in the same code (84, 65, 816, 666) and two digit corrections in the 188 glosses (937, 387, 1019); gist be7b2e6b, CC BY 4.0.

gaps.detail: only 1118 occurs elsewhere (mssBLA 194, glossed 'tain', no sense yet in the report); no new code on the unread pages and no printed clear text found (11 Nov 2026); slot-and-context proposals in beling/results/open_group_values.md, all [?]

texts.label: Report, mssBLA 191 p. 5
texts.summary: An undated report from Port Sainte-Marie to a Milord, in the code of the 1729 sibling letters: thanks for a letter, an answer at the first address, Mr Keene who tells the writer nothing, an accommodement, and a request to be told what to do. Decoded with many holes, not read.

outcome.notes: Key partly recovered, text not read (README Conventions: a key can be obtained while the text is not read). Unfinished: see NOTES.md. 11 Nov 2026 (Andrew Beling, beling/): the code table passed two pre-registered held-out checks (4 Aug clear copy 158/170; mssBLA 194 glosses 89/93); no printed clear text of the report found; the open groups stay open.
